blocks.text: Cotopaxi, Ecuador: a snow-covered summit and clouds above the forest
Cathedral and people in a square beside flowering trees, Quito, Ecuador
Quito: the cathedral's white bell tower above the city square

After breakfast, leave Quito and head north past the Mitad del Mundo monument and the equator. The road then turns west towards the Pacific slopes of the Andes.

The first planned stop is a viewpoint overlooking the extinct Pululahua volcano. Continue to the Tulipe Archaeological Museum. The drive to Tulipe takes about two hours. Here you'll learn about the Yumbo people and see the surviving pools and other structures they built.

From Tulipe, it is about another hour and a half to the entrance to the Mashpi Reserve. The reserve covers roughly 1,300 hectares and has exceptionally rich biodiversity. The scenery changes along the way. The highlands give way to dense forest, and the air grows more humid.

You'll reach the lodge at about 12:00–12:30. On arrival, enjoy a refreshing welcome drink, get help settling in and attend a short introduction. There is a little free time before lunch.

After lunch, the nature programme begins. Activities depend on the group size, the participants' fitness and the weather. At Mashpi, the day's schedule adapts to conditions in the forest and to what guests can comfortably do. If the weather is suitable, you may be able to take an evening walk after dinner.

You'll stay in a 34 m² Wayra Room. The lodge has 19 of these rooms, 15 with double beds. Some rooms interconnect, which can suit families or groups of friends. Rooms have a wardrobe, safe, bathroom, hairdryer, tables, chairs and other furnishings, as well as bathrobes and slippers.

**Accommodation:** Mashpi Lodge, Wayra Room.  
**Meals:** breakfast, lunch and dinner.
